# Recon Tool Test — qbsco.net

All tools were run from the `attackbot/subdomain-wildcards-tools:latest` Docker image
against the target `qbsco.net`. Each tool runs **in parallel**, and its output is
appended to this file **as soon as that tool finishes**.

> Notes:
> - `chaos`, `github-subdomains`, `github-endpoints` require API keys
>   (`PDCP_API_KEY` / `GITHUB_TOKEN`). They were run without keys, so their
>   output shows the key-requirement error.
> - Long-running tools (amass, bbot, waymore, waybackurls, gau) were given a
>   timeout so the test stays practical. Empty output usually means the upstream
>   API (e.g. Wayback CDX) was slow/rate-limited at run time.

---


---

## github-subdomains

**Target:** `qbsco.net`  
**Command:** `github-subdomains -d qbsco.net -q`  
**Status:** exit=255 · 20 lines · 2s  
**Raw output:** `tool_outputs_qbsco/github-subdomains.txt`

```text
Usage of github-subdomains:
  -d string
    	domain you are looking for (required)
  -e	extended mode, also look for <dummy>example.com
  -k	exit the program when all tokens have been disabled
  -o string
    	output file, default: <domain>.txt
  -q	quick mode, avoid extra searches with languages and noise added
  -raw
    	raw output
  -t string
    	github token (required), can be:
    	  • a single token
    	  • a list of tokens separated by comma
    	  • a file (.tokens) containing 1 token per line
    	if the options is not provided, the environment variable GITHUB_TOKEN is readed, it can be:
    	  • a single token
    	  • a list of tokens separated by comma

token not found
```

  -k	exit the program when all tokens have been disabled
  -o string

  -r	display relative urls, default=false
  -raw
    	raw output
  -t string
    	github token (required), can be:

    	  • a list of tokens separated by comma
    	  • a file (.tokens) containing 1 token per line
